draft.title: Sustaining an argument
card: A thesis states the writer's position. Each body paragraph then develops one part of that position.
A topic sentence opens a body paragraph. It names the paragraph's main point and links back to the thesis, often by repeating its main ideas in new words.
The rest of the paragraph stays on that point. Evidence and analysis support the topic sentence, so nothing drifts away from the thesis.
The paragraphs also link to each other. Each one can build on the last, for example by adding a new reason or a stronger consequence, so the argument grows instead of repeating.
draft.remember: Every topic sentence points back to the thesis and moves the argument forward.

a.q: What is the main job of a topic sentence in a body paragraph?
opts: To state the paragraph's point and link it to the thesis
To give a summary of the whole text being studied
To list every piece of evidence the paragraph will use
To restate the question in the writer's own words
a.why: A topic sentence tells the reader what the paragraph will argue and how it connects to the thesis. A plot summary or a list of evidence does not do that, and the evidence belongs later in the paragraph.
a.clue: Think about what links each paragraph to the thesis.

b.q: Zara's thesis is that social media makes teenagers more informed but less focused. Her first paragraph covers being informed. Which topic sentence best opens her second paragraph?
opts: Yet constant alerts also split teenagers' attention
Many teenagers use social media on phones every day
Social media apps began with websites from the 2000s
Teenagers also enjoy videos, games and chatting online
b.why: The first option returns to the 'less focused' half of the thesis and builds on a paragraph about being informed. The others stay on the topic of social media, but they do not develop either part of Zara's position.
b.clue: Which sentence picks up a part of the thesis rather than just the topic?

a.best: To state the paragraph's point and link it to the thesis

b.best: Yet constant alerts also split teenagers' attention

problems.detail: Why (b) calls the right answer 'The first option', but options are shown in random order, so students may be pointed to the wrong sentence. Name the sentence instead, e.g. 'Yet constant alerts also split teenagers' attention'.

The remember line says every topic sentence 'moves the argument forward', but the card only says each paragraph 'can' build on the last. The remember line is firmer than the card.
